RQ1 — Is Thai Internet Good or Bad?

  • Ookla Global Index ranks Thailand fixed broadband #13 worldwide (looks good) -- but ETDA / consumer-complaint surveys report frequent slow/dropped connections (looks bad)
  • Instead of arguing from opinion: cross-validate Ookla (8-country SEA context) and NDT7/M-Lab (independent second data source) against real app-requirement thresholds
  • Thresholds from Lübben & Misfeld (2022), Table 5 -- Voice 64 kbps/200ms · HD 5 Mbps · UHD 25 Mbps · Cloud gaming 44 Mbps + ≤25ms
  • Both platforms measure province-quarter averages -- a structural limitation kept in mind throughout (see Key Findings)

RQ1 — Threshold Pass Rate, All 8 SEA Countries (Ookla Fixed)

% of province-quarters clearing each application threshold, test-weighted, no country highlighted over another.
  • HD (5 Mbps) is a non-issue everywhere -- all 8 countries clear it at 100%
  • UHD (25 Mbps) splits into a real 3-tier gap -- Thailand/Vietnam/Philippines/Singapore/Malaysia all 100%, but Myanmar drops to 20.6%, Cambodia 97.4%, Laos 99.3%
  • Cloud gaming (44 Mbps + <=25ms) is where the region actually differentiates -- only Vietnam and Singapore clear it at 100%; the other 6 countries all show real failures

RQ1 — Cloud-Gaming Threshold Pass Rate by Country (Ookla Fixed)

44 Mbps download + <=25ms latency, test-weighted % of province-quarters passing, all 8 countries.
  • 18.2% of all 2,581 province-quarters SEA-wide fail this threshold -- concentrated in 6 of 8 countries
  • Myanmar 0%, Laos 60.9%, Cambodia 62.8%, Philippines 92.0%, Malaysia 97.5%, Thailand 99.5% -- only Vietnam/Singapore are clean at 100%

RQ1 — Worst Provinces, Cloud-Gaming Failures Across All Countries

Top 15 of 71 provinces (6 countries) by # of quarters (out of 11) failing the cloud-gaming threshold.
  • Worst provinces cluster in Myanmar (8 provinces at 11/11 quarters) and the Philippines' ARMM (11/11) -- remote/historically underserved regions, a last-mile geography story that repeats across borders
  • Thailand's own worst case (Mae Hong Son, 10/11) fits the same pattern at a much smaller scale

RQ1 — Ookla vs NDT7, Thailand & Vietnam Fixed Broadband

NDT7 cross-validation is limited to these 2 countries -- a data-availability constraint (no NDT7 elsewhere), not a scope choice.
  • Fixed broadband agrees closely between platforms in both countries -- HD 100%, UHD 99-100%
  • Cloud-gaming latency fails 0% pass in NDT7 for both countries -- a platform-infrastructure artifact (no in-country M-Lab server), not a real network problem in either

RQ1 — NDT7 Mobile UHD Pass Rate by Province (Where Mobile Actually Degrades)

% of province-quarters clearing the 25 Mbps UHD threshold, NDT7 mobile, ranked by test volume.
  • Bangkok metro cluster underperforms: Bangkok Metropolis, Nonthaburi, Samut Prakan, Pathum Thani clear UHD only 55-67% of the time -- each on a solid multi-quarter sample
  • Chiang Mai and Chon Buri (comparably large samples) sit at 100% -- inverts the usual "rural underserved" framing; the capital metro is where mobile degrades, plausibly congestion
  • First result across both platforms that plausibly supports the "internet feels bad" side of the RQ1 tension

RQ1 — Key Findings

  • HD is trivial everywhere; UHD splits 5-vs-3 -- Myanmar/Cambodia/Laos (lower-income tier) separate from the other 5 countries
  • Cloud gaming is the real differentiator -- 6 of 8 countries show failures, from Myanmar's 0% to Thailand's 99.5%; only Vietnam/Singapore are clean
  • Failures cluster geographically within every affected country -- remote/upland/historically underserved provinces, the same story repeating across borders (Myanmar's ethnic states, Thailand's Mae Hong Son, Philippines' ARMM)
  • Province-quarter averages structurally can't see the ETDA-complaint side of RQ1 in the 5 clean countries -- complaints are almost certainly about tail behavior/reliability, not average-quarter speed
  • NDT7's 0%-everywhere cloud-gaming-latency floor holds in both countries with NDT7 data -- strengthens the read that it's a platform artifact, not evidence about either country's network

RQ2 — What's the Trend?

  • RQ1 asked a snapshot question; RQ2 asks the time dimension across 12 quarters (2023Q1-2025Q4)
  • Part A -- SEA-wide, 8 countries, equal footing: the primary regional trend answer, no country highlighted
  • Part B -- Thailand & Vietnam platform deep-dive (Ookla vs NDT7): limited to these 2 countries because NDT7 data doesn't exist elsewhere -- a data-availability constraint, not a scope choice

RQ2 — Quarterly Download Trend, All 8 SEA Countries (Ookla Fixed)

Median download (Mbps) per quarter, 8 countries, equal color weighting -- no country highlighted.
  • Every country grows -- none flat or declining, from Philippines +23.6% to Myanmar +163.8%
  • Thailand's +42.0% is 2nd-slowest, but a high-base/catch-up story: Thailand's absolute level stays 2nd-highest of 8 throughout, behind only Singapore

RQ2 — SEA Growth-Context Findings

  • Fastest-growing 4 (Myanmar, Cambodia, Vietnam, Laos) all start from a much lower 2023 base (20-92 Mbps) -- classic catch-up growth
  • Singapore breaks the base-effect story -- the only country starting above Thailand (282 Mbps), yet still posts +96.4% growth, more than double Thailand's rate
  • Malaysia is the sharpest open question -- growing nearly 2x faster than Thailand from a lower base, flagged for the Discussion section (infrastructure-investment timing, not just diminishing returns)

RQ2 — Growth by Region, Thailand (Ookla Fixed)

Median & mean download growth by region, 2023Q1 → 2025Q4.
  • Northern +49%/+46% leads; Central +30%/+32% trails.

RQ2 — Growth by Region, Vietnam (Ookla Fixed)

Median & mean download growth by region, 2023Q1 → 2025Q4.
  • Remarkably uniform across all 8 regions -- 119-132% median growth, no clear leader/laggard.

RQ2 — Growth by Region, Philippines (Ookla Fixed)

Median & mean download growth by region, 2023Q1 → 2025Q4.
  • Grouped by island (Luzon/Visayas/Mindanao) rather than the 17 official regions -- coarser granularity than the other 7 countries' charts.

RQ2 — Growth by Region, Singapore (Ookla Fixed)

Median & mean download growth by region, 2023Q1 → 2025Q4.
  • All 5 regions are single-province -- median and mean collapse to the same point. Illustrative, not statistically robust.

RQ2 — Growth by Region, Cambodia (Ookla Fixed)

Median & mean download growth by region, 2023Q1 → 2025Q4.
  • North leads at +195%; several regions backed by only 1-3 provinces -- thin-sample caveat applies.

RQ2 — Growth by Region, Laos (Ookla Fixed)

Median & mean download growth by region, 2023Q1 → 2025Q4.
  • Central leads (+128% median); reasonable province counts (5-8) per region.

RQ2 — Growth by Region, Malaysia (Ookla Fixed)

Median & mean download growth by region, 2023Q1 → 2025Q4.
  • Tight spread (70-80%) across all 5 regions -- no standout leader or laggard.

RQ2 — Growth by Region, Myanmar (Ookla Fixed)

Median & mean download growth by region, 2023Q1 → 2025Q4.
  • Eastern Highlands +246% (n=2) is an extreme swing off a tiny base -- read as illustrative given n=2.

RQ2 — Part B: Thailand & Vietnam Platform Deep-Dive

  • Four segments: Ookla fixed/mobile, NDT7 fixed/mobile -- limited to Thailand (all four) because NDT7 doesn't exist for the other 6 countries
  • Covers Ookla-vs-NDT7 trend agreement and a province-level drilldown (Bangkok metro mobile) that only this data supports

RQ2 — Quarterly Download Trend, Thailand 2023Q1-2025Q4

Median download (Mbps) per quarter, IQR shaded, 4 segments.
  • Ookla fixed: steady near-linear growth, 207 → 294 Mbps (+42%) -- the least-noisy series here
  • Ookla mobile: flat through 2023 (~55-60), then a real inflection from 2024-Q2, reaching 91-104 Mbps by 2025 -- consistent with a 5G-rollout story
  • NDT7 fixed tracks the same upward direction (+56%) despite a ~3x lower absolute level (single-TCP-stream, lower-bound methodology)

RQ2 — Quarterly Upload Trend, Thailand 2023Q1-2025Q4

Median upload (Mbps) per quarter, IQR shaded, 4 segments.
  • Same shape as download, smaller magnitude -- Ookla fixed +35%, NDT7 fixed +63%, both monotonically up
  • Ookla mobile flat at ~17 Mbps through 2023-2024, then rises to 23-25 Mbps in 2025 -- echoes the download inflection, supports the 5G read
  • NDT7 mobile upload is noisy with no trend (thin-sample segment)

RQ2 — Quarterly Latency Trend, Thailand 2023Q1-2025Q4

Median latency (ms) per quarter, IQR shaded, 25ms cloud-gaming ceiling marked.
  • Ookla fixed flat at 8-10ms the entire 3 years -- already far under the ceiling, nothing to improve
  • Ookla mobile holds 30-36ms, hovering just above the ceiling, at most a marginal dip late 2025
  • NDT7 (fixed and mobile) stays 60-120ms for all 12 quarters, never once approaching 25ms -- confirms RQ1's latency floor is a persistent M-Lab server-placement artifact, not a transient or improving last-mile issue

RQ2 — Bangkok Metro Mobile: A 2023 Problem That Resolved

  • Headline result of the Thailand/Vietnam deep-dive (Part B), not of RQ2 as a whole -- Part A's SEA-wide growth comparison is the region-level answer
  • RQ1's pooled 55-67% UHD pass rate for Bangkok metro hid a sharp step change: 0-7% through all of 2023, then a clean jump to 100% every quarter from 2024-Q1 onward
  • Not an ongoing problem -- already resolved by the time of writing (mid-2025)

RQ2 — Key Findings

  • Part A (SEA-wide): every country grows, no exceptions; Thailand's 2nd-slowest % growth is a high-base story, not stagnation -- absolute level stays 2nd-highest of 8 throughout
  • Part A region-level: growth is broad-based within every country, not driven by one region alone
  • Part B (Thailand & Vietnam): download/upload monotonic growth on all platforms with data; NDT7's latency floor never approaches the 25ms ceiling in either country across 3 years -- persistent platform artifact, not a national problem
  • Part B headline: Bangkok metro mobile's RQ1 "underperforms" finding was a 2023-only problem, resolved by 2024-Q1
